validity.recommendation: no action — existence, classification, fuel/fuel-source, length and endpoints all corroborate
validity.researcher_notes: Existence CONFIRMED by three independent non-GEM sources, none derived from the gem.wiki page: (1) Kurskaya Encyclopedia (mke.su) — 'ГАЗОПРОВОД «Шебелинка – Белгород – Курск – Брянск» — транспортный трубопровод по доставке газа из Шебелинского газового месторождения... в областные центры России — Белгород, Курск и Брянск'; (2) Ukrainian Wikipedia (uk.wikipedia.org, article title 'Шебелинка — Білгород — Курськ — Брянськ (ШБКБ)') — same route, describes it as one of the pipelines built to move gas from the giant Shebelinka field in Kharkiv Oblast to Belgorod/Kursk/Bryansk, ending in Bryansk; (3) Interfax (2022) reports Gazprom's reconstruction of a section of this exact pipeline (named there 'Шебелинка-Брянск-Курск-Белгород', same route/abbreviation ШБКБ, word order only differs), with Rostekhnadzor sign-off 27 Oct 2022 — i.e. the asset is real, named, and under active engineering work as of 2022. Classification (PipelineType=transmission) matches — described as a 'транспортний трубопровід' (transport/trunk pipeline), not a gathering/feeder line. Fuel=Gas and FuelSource='Shebelinskoe gas field' both confirm against mke.su and uk.wikipedia (both independently name the Shebelinske/Шебелинское gas field, Kharkiv Oblast, as origin). Length=507.00 km CONFIRMED independently — uk.wikipedia states 'Довжина траси газопроводу становить 507 км' (the route length is 507 km), matching GEM exactly and NOT sourced from GEM. Location/endpoints CONFIRMED: StartLocation=Shebelinka (Kharkiv Oblast, Ukraine) and end in Bryansk (Bryansk Oblast, Russia) both stated explicitly by mke.su and uk.wikipedia; GEM's EndLocation cell was blank — filled below (see fills[]).

validity.recommendation: correct StartYear1 from 1960 to 1959 (or 1958 if the Belgorod-only milestone is preferred)
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records StartYear1=1960, but THREE independent non-GEM sources put this pipeline's own commissioning a year earlier and none supports 1960: Kurskaya Encyclopedia (mke.su) — 'В июле 1959 г. состоялось окончание работ по прокладке' (pipe-laying completed July 1959) and 'В ноябре-декабре 1959 г. началась эксплуатация' (industrial operation began Nov-Dec 1959); Spravochnick.ru — construction 'Completed in 1959; в этом же году началось его промышленное использование' (industrial use began that same year, 1959); Ukrainian Wikipedia — gas reached Belgorod already in 1958 ('сюди ресурс надійшов вже у 1958-му'), with the line completed to Bryansk in the late 1950s. The ONLY appearance of '1960' in any source is for a DIFFERENT, unrelated event: uk.wikipedia states the southern section of the SEPARATE Dashava-Kyiv-Bryansk-Moscow pipeline was reversed so Shebelinka gas could reach Kyiv from 1960 ('шебелинський газ зміг надходити до Києва з 1960-го, ще до завершення прямого газопроводу Шебелинка – Київ') — that is about Kyiv supply via a different trunk, not this pipeline's own construction date. GEM's 1960 looks like a conflation of the two facts. This is a material date discrepancy, not a rounding difference.

validity.recommendation: record as a multi-value diameter (700, 800, 1020 mm) per the tracker's multi-value convention, or add a ResearcherNotes caveat — do not overwrite the sheet with a single figure
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's single Diameter=1020mm is technically one of the real diameters on this system but materially UNDERSTATES it: per Ukrainian Wikipedia, the system was built as two parallel lines — 'Первісно тут проклали нитку діаметром 700 мм (трубопровід ШБКБ I), яку невдовзі доповнили другою ниткою в діаметрі 800 мм (ШБКБ ІІ). В подальшому ШБКБ ІІ підсилили лупінгом діаметром 1020 мм' (originally a 700mm line [ShBKB I], soon supplemented by an 800mm second line [ShBKB II], later reinforced by a 1020mm looping) — i.e. three different diameters across the corridor's history, not one pipe. A FOURTH, newer diameter is also documented: Interfax (2022, Rostekhnadzor-approved reconstruction) and Spravochnick.ru both describe a new ~44km bypass/loop built 2020-2022 at ~1200mm (uk.wikipedia gives 1220mm for the same new loop: 'лупінгом довжиною 44 км та діаметром 1220 мм'). So the corridor now carries at least four historical diameters (700/800/1020/~1200mm) across parallel threads, and a bare '1020' materially undersells the asset even though it isn't 'wrong' per se.

validity.recommendation: do not carry Gazprom PJSC 100% for the whole cross-border line — split ownership by section; verify the Ukrainian-side operator name (likely Gas TSO of Ukraine / TSOU-GTSOU, tsoua.com, currently 403ing to automated fetches) before writing a replacement value
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Owner1='Gazprom PJSC' 100% for a pipeline whose own recorded endpoints span StartCountryOrArea=Ukraine (Shebelinka) to EndCountryOrArea=Russia (Bryansk Oblast) — i.e. a genuinely cross-border asset. Per this project's standing Ukraine guidance, Gazprom does not own any Ukrainian section of the GTS (state-owned since independence; TSOU/GTSOU operates it since 1 Jan 2020, Ukrtransgaz before that) — a 100%-Gazprom reading is only correct if the row is meant to describe the Russian section alone. Independent corroboration that the two halves are administratively and operationally distinct: Ukrainian Wikipedia states plainly 'Наразі українська та російська ділянки системи працюють окремо' (currently the Ukrainian and Russian sections of the system operate SEPARATELY), and that the Ukrainian portion (together with the separate Shebelinka-Kharkiv line) primarily supplies Kharkiv — i.e. it is not a single Gazprom-run asset end to end. I could not independently confirm a specific Ukrainian-side operator/owner name for this exact line (tsoua.com returned HTTP 403 to all fetch attempts, consistent with the known WAF issue) — flagging the concern without proposing a specific replacement name to avoid fabricating an owner.

No duplicate/relabel risk: P3381/P3382 ('Shebelinka-Slovyansk') share the Shebelinka origin but terminate at Slovyansk, a wholly different destination and a much shorter route (70km/54km vs 507km) — clearly a separate, distinct line, not a segment of P2387. None of the other roster rows (P1480, P3063, P3484, P5935, P5938, P5989) share either endpoint or name with P2387.

fills.researcher_notes: GEM's Location group had EndState/Province='Bryansk Oblast' and EndCountryOrArea='Russia' filled but EndLocation itself blank. Both mke.su ('...в областные центры России — Белгород, Курск и Брянск') and uk.wikipedia ('...завершувався у Брянську') independently confirm the line terminates at the city of Bryansk itself, so filling EndLocation='Bryansk' with these two independent refs.

summary: Real, well-documented Soviet-era trunk (confirmed by 3 independent non-GEM sources incl. 2022 Interfax reconstruction reporting); 507km length and classification/fuel/fuelsource/endpoints all corroborate and EndLocation blank filled with 'Bryansk'. Three concerns staged: StartYear1 should be 1959 not 1960 (GEM appears to conflate this line's own commissioning with an unrelated 1960 Kyiv-reversal event on a different pipeline); Diameter=1020mm materially understates a 700/800/1020(+~1200 new loop) multi-thread system; Owner1=Gazprom PJSC 100% is doubtful for this cross-border asset since Ukrainian and Russian sections are independently confirmed to operate separately (no duplicate-owner name proposed — avoiding fabrication).
